statement: You are given a singly linked list whose node values, read from head to tail, are listed in values. If loopPos is −1 the tail points to null; otherwise the tail's next pointer goes back to the node at 0-based position loopPos.
The algorithm sees only the head. If the list has a loop, find the node where the loop begins: the first node you reach from the head that is part of the loop.
Return the value of that node, or null if the list has no loop.

examples.explanation: The tail −4 links back to the node at position 1, so the loop is 2 → 0 → −4 → 2 and it begins at the node holding 2.
The tail points to null, so there is no loop and no starting node.

constraints: The number of nodes is in the range [0, 10⁴]
loopPos is −1 or a valid index in the list
